geometry_edits.rationale: Replace the folded roof with a simpler sectional profile that better expresses a gymnasium hall and daylight logic.
Preserve the long-span direction along the dominant bar so the hall remains legible in section.
Turn the existing carve toward the access side to strengthen the entry seam and public ground response.

graph_edits.rationale: Simplify the roof/section toward a clearer long-span reading while keeping the dominant elongated hall gesture.
Maintain the longitudinal hall emphasis and reduce the ambiguity of the section.
Align the public threshold carve with the verified access side to make the ground response more legible.

rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent early-stage gymnasium massing: a single low elongated body with one dominant roof/section idea and a central carved void that gives the plan some public logic. It responds to the parcel reasonably well and stays inside the boundary in all views, so it clears the hard containment gate. The blue frontage edge is answered only weakly: there is a void/seam near the edge, but it is not yet a strongly public or unmistakably welcoming access figure. The main weakness is sectional: the roof is folded and stepped, but the section does not yet clearly express a long-span hall with a subordinate support bar; it still feels somewhat generic and slightly over-articulated. Still, the mass is legible across all views and does not show obvious view-to-view collision, so it remains acceptable as a gymnasium concept.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Long, low sports volume with a clear sectional roof gesture and a grounded public edge.
Legible hall massing with a stronger public threshold and a coherent roof datum.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Courtyard/void as a civic sports response; useful for public ground articulation.
